pairs.why: A shows the stone table up close and chunky, filling the frame like the real card does; B is a small far-off object in a busy park, though its square block base with cracks is closer in detail.
Both add an orange band the real light doesn't have, but A is bigger, fills the frame and has the same heavy dark-metal mass as the real fixture; B is smaller and fussier.
A hangs flat on the striped wall with a soft drop shadow like the real clock; B stands upright on a floor, which changes how the object is built and staged.
A's dome is large and fills the frame like the real buildings; B's base is small inside an empty landscape, though the two are rendered about the same.
A matches the real light's dark navy metal on a teal haze, with no extra orange band or gold knob; its boxy yoke is the only weaker point.
B's fabric wraps around the tubes as sleeves on both seat and back, built like the real camp chair; A's seat ends at a bare front bar and its back panel hangs loose.
A is a solid, glossy 3D hat with a curled brim and a badge band, like the chunky real items; B is flat and stiff, with an odd cream rim on the brim.
B has the riveted metal bands, chrome-ringed portholes, thruster flame and lively diagonal pose of the real submarine; A is plainer and stiffer.
